messages:
Priya S: Customer (org: AcmeHealth) opened a ticket — since 04:15 UTC they're seeing 401s and +150ms tail latency. They say requests that should go to us-west are hitting eu-central.
Jordan R: grabbing logs now. Do we have a recent routing config change? :mag:
deploy-bot: deploy event: routes/policies updated by Alex P @ 2026-02-11T04:14:38Z (commit 9f3a7c2)
Alex P: That matching change was a small UI fix for the policy editor; didn't touch runtime sorting intentionally. I pushed config that renames priority keys to strings to support UI ordering.
Sam L: can you paste the affected failover policy JSON from the customer? I want to see priority keys.
Priya S: Paste from ticket:

```
"failover_policy": {
  "priority": {
    "1": { "region": "us-west", "weight": 70, "sticky": true },
    "10": { "region": "eu-central", "weight": 30, "sticky": false },
    "2": { "region": "us-east", "weight": 0, "sticky": false }
  },
  "fallback_order": ["1","10","2"]
}
```

Priya S: Customer said they originally authored priorities as ints; UI saved them as strings.
Jordan R: aha. Runtime currently enumerates priority keys and sorts them to build ordered list. It looks like keys are being sorted lexicographically ("10" before "2") which would reorder priorities to 1,10,2 -> that still seems odd, but if string sorting is used elsewhere it might pick the wrong primary when weights/ttl combine.
Sam L: I can repro locally. If keys are strings, our sort comparator uses default JS object key order in the UI -> some paths treat keys as strings and call .sort() without numeric coercion. Repro steps:

1) POST policy with string keys as above
2) Query route-eval endpoint: `curl -H "x-api-key: <key>" https://api.redwood-inference/v1/route-eval?model=gpt-j`
3) observe `selected_region: eu-central` for ~12% of requests (based on the weight calc bug)

Sam L: relevant log snippet:

```
[route-eval] request_id=ab12 selected_candidates=["1","10","2"]
[route-eval] sorted_by_priority=["1","10","2"] // expected numeric [1,2,10]
[route-eval] chosen=10 // wrong due to weight tie-handling and lexicographic key ordering
```

Alex P: I see — when keys are strings, our tiebreak path calls parseInt only for bucket computations but not for initial ordering. That means '10' can end up ahead of '2' in internal arrays used by the weighting algorithm.
Maria K: Customer reported auth service in eu-central is rejecting API keys (401) for their account; they were surprised because us-west had the keys. Also billing jump from cross-region egress.
Priya S: CS note: AcmeHealth is on a compliance plan, egress to eu region is a contract violation — they escalated. We need mitigation ASAP.
Jordan R: Immediate mitigation: we can patch the customer policy to convert keys back to numeric indices. I can run a CLI edit and push a corrected policy while eng provides a runtime fix.
Sam L: I'll open a hotfix PR to coerce priority keys to Number when parsing JSON in the route-eval path. PR: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/4823 (hotfix). Will push a canary to staging then prod if green.
Alex P: For immediate rollback, Jordan — run this command to rewrite the customer's policy to numeric keys (tested):

```
redwoodctl policies set --org acmehealth --policy-id pf-782 --file ./pf-782-normalized.json
```

where pf-782-normalized.json has numeric priority array form:

```
"priority": [
  {"index": 1, "region": "us-west", "weight": 70, "sticky": true},
  {"index": 2, "region": "us-east", "weight": 0, "sticky": false},
  {"index": 10, "region": "eu-central", "weight": 30, "sticky": false}
]
```

Jordan R: Doing the rewrite now. Will watch logs and QoS.
deploy-bot: policy update applied for org=acmehealth policy=pf-782 @ 2026-02-11T04:22:10Z
Jordan R: After rewrite, route-eval shows selected_region=us-west for 88% requests. Tail latency back to baseline, auth 401s drop.
Priya S: Customer confirmed less 401s within 6 minutes and reduced latency. CS notified customer and offered 3 months of bill credit for egress overage. :white_check_mark:
Sam L: Hotfix merged to main, patch will coerce numeric ordering and add a unit test for string keys. Will also add a migration check in the Console UI to warn when saving string-indexed priority maps.
Alex P: Filed follow-ups: UI change to save numeric arrays, add server-side validation. Created issue INF-1298.
Maria K: Thanks team. For postmortem, tag severity P2 and include contract breach note. I'll draft the postmortem.
customer-success-bot: AcmeHealth notified, ticket updated #T-40321.
Priya S: Closing thread once postmortem and billing remediation are confirmed. :raised_hands:
